title: Loginly — Account Recovery
objective: You may make a limited number of requests before this account is locked out. Find the correct 2-digit recovery code.

verifier.condition: More operations than the per-request limit are executed within a single HTTP request and the correct code is found among them.

weakness: The account is locked out after 5 HTTP requests, counted by incrementing a counter once per incoming POST — but GraphQL array/batch requests let one POST carry many separate operations, each executed and none of them separately counted against the limit.
seededData: A logged-in account with a synthetic 2-digit recovery code generated per instance. In memory; reset with the instance.

credentials.label: Customer
credentials.note: Can make a limited number of guesses per request.

hints: Make a few guesses the normal way and find out exactly how the limit is enforced — what triggers it, and what does not.
A GraphQL request does not have to contain only one query. Look into what a JSON array in the request body does.
Send one POST whose body is an array of every possible 2-digit code as separate operations.
burpNotes: Build the batched array request in Repeater; a script that generates all 10,000 combinations across a handful of large batches is the practical approach.
